[Frackingiscool] They can indeed. I bought a fair few last year on Amazon for $47 each and they are in my tablets, handhelds, raspberry pi, and 2 in security cameras.
I hate that I don't need one but want one because it's cheapest price for a reliable brand card with the voucher. Even garbage brand cards on Amazon cost more.
[ThemDealsThough] Weirdly though, you can only get the speeds of this card with a micro sd express adapter. Otherwise it drops to UH-I speeds rather than dropping to UH-II speeds. Which is really slow.
[viper8548] does this mean it will be super slow on a non micro sd express device?
[ThemDealsThough] Unless the device reads micro sd express cards (basically the Switch 2) this will act like a UH-i card. So your better of getting a UH-ii card which writes and reads at about 300mbs rather than dropping down to the 100mbs with UH-i
[GreenLego] @viper8548: UHS-II has extra row of 8 pins (total of 16). In the microSD Express, that extra row is replaced by 9 pins (total of 17) to make it PCIe. There's not enough room to have UHS-II pins and PCIe pins at the same time.
[Proliferation] UHS-II Micro SD cards have two rows of contacts, like SD Express, but my guess is that since SD Express is based on PCIe the signalling isn't backwards compatible and so those extra pads are disabled or simply go unused when you put an Express card in an older device.
This is also assuming your device has a micro SD card slot with two rows of pins, and it probably doesn't unless it was very expensive (which UHS-II micro SD cards are well, attracting a premium of like ~3-5x the cost of a UHS-I card of the same capacity).
Edit: Also worth noting that Express cards use slightly more power during read/write operations than normal micro SDs, so they're actually kind of worse unless you're using one in an Express-capable device.
[cheap4321] Good for security cams that continuously overwrite?
[aragornelessar] You'll want an endurance card for continual writes.
[dna level c] This is correct.
And make sure that you register your cards with the manufacturer and keep your receipts for warranty purposes.
